title: Binding Sites of a Positron Emission Tomography Radioligand with Nanomolar Affinity to Alpha-Synuclein Fibrils
content: Diagnosing neurodegenerative diseases currently depends on a physician’s interpretation of neurological symptoms. However, because these symptoms often overlap across disorders, patients may be misdiagnosed or only correctly diagnosed after years of ineffective treatment [1]. Additionally, some clinical symptoms only emerge in the later stages of the disease. This challenge is especially pronounced for synucleinopathies, such as Parkinson’s Disease (PD), Multiple Systems Atrophy (MSA), and Lewy Body Dementia (LBD), all of which are associated with the overexpression or aggregation of α-synuclein in neurons and glia [2]. Unfortunately, no definitive diagnostic test currently exists for these conditions. The lack of diagnostic tools is particularly concerning given that PD is the second most common neurodegenerative disorder in the U.S. after Alzheimer’s disease (AD), for which a reliable diagnostic blood test is currently being developed [3]. A recent study has shown that the use of skin biopsies to detect phosphorylated α-synuclein could aide in the diagnosis of synucleinopathies, though it remains in early development [4]. As a result, the urgent need for reliable diagnostic tools has spurred significant interest in developing early detection techniques based on disease-specific biomarkers.
